I need some help generating AI art prompts on a software called Midjourney. First, I
am going to explain what Midjourney is and what it can do. Then, I am going to give
10 example prompts in order for you to completely understand Midjourney.
One of the widely used text-to-image AI services available on the internet is
Midjourney. Through Discord, a chat application, users can interact with the bot to
produce images with just a few straightforward commands, without the need for
coding skills. The results are visually attractive images that are easy to create.
You can Interact with the Midjourney Bot on Discord using a {{glossary.Command}}.
Commands are used to create images, change default settings, monitor user info,
and perform other helpful tasks.
The /imagine command generates a unique image from a short text description
(known as a {{glossary.Prompt}}).
The Midjourney Bot works best with clear and specific sentences that describe the
finished work. It does not work well with conversational style lists of requests. Rather
than providing specific instructions, such as 'Show me a picture of lots of blooming
California poppies, make them bright, vibrant orange, and draw them in an
illustrated style with colored pencils,' try describing what you want in a more
straightforward manner, such as 'Vibrant orange California poppies illustrated with
colored pencils.
Generating an image activates the free Midjourney trial.Trial users can make roughly
25 Jobs before needing to subscribe. A Job is any action that uses the Midjourney
Bot. Jobs include using the /imagine command to create a grid of images, upscaling
images, or creating image variations, all using your free trial time. Use the /info
command to check your Fast Time Remaining to see your remaining Trial time.
Here are some prompting notes:
Prompt Length
Prompts can be very simple. Single words (or even an emoji!) will produce an image.
Very short prompts will rely heavily on Midjourney’s default style, so a more
descriptive prompt is better for a unique look. However, super-long prompts aren’t
always better. Concentrate on the main concepts you want to create.
Grammar
The Midjourney Bot does not understand grammar, sentence structure, or words like
humans. Word choice also matters. More specific synonyms work better in many
circumstances. Instead of big, try gigantic, enormous, or immense. Remove words
when possible. Fewer words mean each word has a more powerful influence. Use
commas, brackets, and hyphens to help organize your thoughts, but know the
Midjourney Bot will not reliably interpret them. The Midjourney Bot does not
consider capitalization. Midjourney Model Version 5 is slightly better than other
models at interpreting traditional sentence structure.
Focus on What you Want
It is better to describe what you want instead of what you don’t want. If you ask for a
party with “no cake,” your image will probably include a cake. If you want to ensure
an object is not in the final image, try advance prompting using the --no parameter.
Think About What Details Matter
Anything left unsaid may surprise you. Be as specific or vague as you want, but
anything you leave out will be randomized. Being vague is a great way to get variety,
but you may not get the specific details you want.
Try to be clear about any context or details that are important to you. Think
about:
Subject: person, animal, character, location, object, etc.
Medium: photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle, tapestry, etc.
Environment: indoors, outdoors, on the moon, in Narnia, underwater, the Emerald
City, etc.
Lighting: soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio lights, etc
Color: vibrant, muted, bright, monochromatic, colorful, black and white, pastel, etc.
Mood: Sedate, calm, raucous, energetic, etc.
Composition: Portrait, headshot, closeup, birds-eye view, etc.
Use Collective Nouns
Plural words leave a lot to chance. Try specific numbers. "Three cats" is more specific
than "cats." Collective nouns also work, “flock of birds” instead of "birds.”
Parameters Available
Aspect Ratios
--aspect, or --ar Change the aspect ratio of a generation.
Chaos
--chaos <number 0–100> Change how varied the results will be. Higher values
produce more unusual and unexpected generations.
No
--no Negative prompting, --no plants would try to remove plants from the image.
Quality
--quality <.25, .5, 1, or 2>, or --q <.25, .5, 1, or 2> How much rendering quality time you
want to spend. The default value is 1. Higher values cost more and lower values cost
less.
Repeat
--repeat <1–40>, or --r <1–40> Create multiple Jobs from a single prompt. --repeat is
useful for quickly rerunning a job multiple times.
Seed
--seed <integer between 0–4294967295> The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to
create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the
initial image grids. Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be
specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter. Using the same seed number
and prompt will produce similar ending images.
Stop
--stop <integer between 10–100> Use the --stop parameter to finish a Job partway
through the process. Stopping a Job at an earlier percentage can create blurrier, less
detailed results.
Style
--style <4a, 4b, or 4c> Switch between versions of the Midjourney Model Version 4
--style <expressive, or cute> Switch between versions of the Niji Model Version 5
Stylize
--stylize <number>, or --s <number> parameter influences how strongly Midjourney's
default aesthetic style is applied to Jobs.
Uplight
--uplight Use an alternative "light" upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results
are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image is less detailed and
smoother.
Upbeta
--upbeta Use an alternative beta upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results
are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image has significantly fewer
added details.
Midjourney routinely releases new model versions to improve efficiency, coherency,
and quality. Different models excel at different types of images.
Niji
--niji An alternative model focused on anime style images.
High Definition
--hd Use an early alternative Model that produces larger, less consistent images. This
algorithm may be suitable for abstract and landscape images.
Test
--test Use the Midjourney special test model.
Testp
--testp Use the Midjourney special photography-focused test model.
Version
--version <1, 2, 3, 4, or 5> or --v <1, 2, 3, 4, or 5> Use a different version of the Midjourney
algorithm. The current algorithm (V4) is the default setting.

self.load_protocols()

self.protocol_list.grid(column=0, row=1, sticky=(tk.W, tk.N, tk.E, tk.S))
self.protocol_list.bind(’<<ListboxSelect>>‘, self.update_protocol_view)

# Add protocol button
ttk.Button(self.protocol_list_frame, text=‘Add Protocol’, command=self.new_protocol_window).grid(column=0, row=2, pady=10)

# Sequence protocol view frame
self.protocol_view_frame = ttk.Frame(self.main_frame)
self.protocol_view_frame.grid(column=1, row=0, padx=10, pady=10, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E, tk.N, tk.S))

ttk.Label(self.protocol_view_frame, text=‘Protocol Name:’).grid(column=0, row=0, sticky=(tk.W))
self.protocol_name_var = tk.StringVar()
self.protocol_name_entry = ttk.Entry(self.protocol_view_frame, textvariable=self.protocol_name_var)
self.protocol_name_entry.grid(column=1, row=0, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E))

ttk.Label(self.protocol_view_frame, text=‘Sequences:’).grid(column=0, row=1, sticky=(tk.W))
self.sequence_tree = ttk.Treeview(self.protocol_view_frame, height=8, columns=3)
self.sequence_tree.grid(column=1, row=1, sticky=(tk.W, tk.E, tk.N, tk.S))
self.sequence_tree.column(“#0”, width=0, stretch=tk.NO)
self.sequence_tree.column(1, width=150, minwidth=100)
self.sequence_tree.column(2, width=150, minwidth=100)
self.sequence_tree.column(3, width=150, minwidth=100)
self.sequence_tree.heading(1, text=‘Sequence Type’)
self.sequence_tree.heading(2, text=‘Orientation’)
self.sequence_tree.heading(3, text=‘Annotation’)

# Save button
ttk.Button(self.protocol_view_frame, text=‘Save Protocol’, command=self.save_protocol).grid(column=1, row=2, pady=10, sticky=(tk.E))

def update_protocol_view(self, event=None):
if self.protocol_list.curselection():
selected_protocol_index = self.protocol_list.curselection()[0]
protocol = self.protocols[selected_protocol_index]

self.protocol_name_var.set(protocol[‘name’])

self.sequence_tree.delete(*self.sequence_tree.get_children())
for i, sequence_data in enumerate(protocol[‘sequences’]):
self.sequence_tree.insert(’‘, ‘end’, text=str(i + 1),
values=(sequence_data[‘type’], sequence_data[‘orientation’], sequence_data[‘annotation’]))

def load_protocols(self):
try:
with open(self.protocol_data_file, ‘rb’) as file:
self.protocols = pickle.load(file)
except FileNotFoundError:
self.protocols = []

for protocol in self.protocols:
self.protocol_list.insert(tk.END, protocol[‘name’])

def save_protocols(self):
with open(self.protocol_data_file, ‘wb’) as file:
pickle.dump(self.protocols, file)

def new_protocol_window(self):
self.new_protocol_win = tk.Toplevel(self)
self.new_protocol_win.title(‘New Protocol’)

ttk.Label(self.new_protocol_win, text=‘Protocol Name:’).grid(column=0, row=0, padx=10, pady=(10, 0))

ttk.Button(self.new_protocol_win, text=‘Add’, command=lambda: self.create_new_protocol(new_name_var.get())).grid(column=1, row=1, pady=10)

def create_new_protocol(self, name):
if not name.strip():
messagebox.showerror(“Error”, “Protocol name cannot be empty.”)
return

new_protocol = {“name”: name, “sequences”: []}
self.protocols.append(new_protocol)
self.protocol_list.insert(tk.END, new_protocol[‘name’])

self.new_protocol_win.destroy()

def save_protocol(self):
selected_protocol_index = self.protocol_list.curselection()[0]
protocol = self.protocols[selected_protocol_index]

protocol[‘name’] = self.protocol_name_var.get().strip()

protocol[‘sequences’] = []
for sequence in self.sequence_tree.get_children():
sequence_data = self.sequence_tree.item(sequence)[‘values’]
protocol[‘sequences’].append({
‘type’: sequence_data[0],
‘orientation’: sequence_data[1],
‘annotation’: sequence_data[2]
})

self.protocol_list.delete(selected_protocol_index)
self.protocol_list.insert(selected_protocol_index, protocol[‘name’])

self.save_protocols()

if name == ‘main’:
app = MRIProtocolsApp()
app.mainloop()

based on this text: "Dear advocate,
As they say, the more things change, the more they remain the same.
In our community of providers, in our society and across the globe, so much has changed in the past
few years. Seismic shifts in the labor market and the broader economy, directly or indirectly the result
of the COVID-19 pandemic, have left us working and thinking differently—for better or worse.
To be sure, the pandemic set in motion some positive shifts in the landscape of services available
to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. New and new uses of technology made
possible the expansion of remote supports, for example, while temporary funding increases enabled
direct support professionals to see the first meaningful increase in median wages in nearly a decade.
Nevertheless, so much remains the same. A dire recruitment and retention crisis in the direct support
workforce looms large. So too do substantial disparities between people of color and white people,
both among people with disabilities and the professionals who make their access to the community
possible. Meanwhile, we continue to see significant deficiencies in our ability to fully understand these
disparities due to an ongoing dearth of data.
If these situations have changed, they have done so only by their order of magnitude. As this year’s
Case for Inclusion illustrates, a situation we have long feared is now being born out in the data: people
with IDD are increasingly unable to access the services they need. At alarming rates, providers are
turning away new referrals and discontinuing existing services due to a lack of staffing. In turn, people
are having to travel significant distances or forgo services altogether because even when their state
approves them to pursue services, too few providers exist to offer them.
That’s why we need decisive action and we need it now. To stem the tide of growing instability in
our service delivery system, it will take lawmakers and regulators at all levels of government, as well
as providers and advocates, working together in lockstep, demonstrating the promise of community
inclusion for all and the power of investing in a qualified workforce to deliver on that promise.
In that spirit, this report and its accompanying online tools are designed to strengthen and support
your advocacy for the direct support workforce and the people they support so we may work together
to build a better future for all of the people who contribute to our communities.
Thank you for being on this journey with us."

Introducing the Glaciwild Region!

Geography:
The Glaciwild Region is centered around the Antarctic Peninsula, stretching from the tropical seas in the north to the frozen tundra further south. Due to unique weather patterns and geographical features, this region has a surprising variety of climates and biomes. It is divided into four main areas:

1. Tropical Strand: A warm, tropical area with beautiful sandy beaches, lush jungles, and crystal-clear waters. This area is home to a variety of water, grass, and bug-type Pokémon, as well as rare regional variants of ice-type Pokémon that have adapted to the hot climate.

2. Boreon Peaks: A mountainous region with chilly weather, breathtaking sights, and rocky terrain. Cave systems and tall peaks make this area a playground for rock, ground, and ice-type Pokémon.

3. Frostvale: A snow-covered valley and the heart of Glaciwild Region civilization. The bustling Frostvale City is the region’s main hub, where trainers can find the Pokémon League, Grand Research Lab, Battle Tower, and an array of festivals and cultural events.

4. Tundraglade: The southernmost and coldest region in Glaciwild, Tundraglade is a vast frozen wasteland with powerful blizzards, glaciers, and ice floes. This area is home to many powerful, rare ice-type Pokémon that can only be found in these extreme conditions.

Culture and History:
Glaciwild Region was initially colonized by people from all over the Pokémon world, making it an incredibly diverse and vibrant culture. This fusion of cultures is seen in everything from the regional cuisine to its architecture and even its Pokémon Trainer styles. Many ancient ruins are scattered throughout the region and are filled with mysteries about the past of Glaciwild.

Pokémon League and Gyms:
The Glaciwild Pokémon League consists of eight gyms, each with a focus on a different Pokémon type. These gym leaders are experts of their respective types and have challenged trainers from all over the region for years:

1. Marina (Water)
2. Oliver (Grass)
3. Ember (Fire)
4. Sylvia (Psychic)
5. Rex (Rock)
6. Skadi (Ice)
7. Finn (Flying)
8. Luna (Dark)

After defeating each gym leader, trainers will face the Elite Four, which consists of champions (each with a mixed team of Pokémon) and the Pokémon Champion. This final challenge will determine who can claim the title of Glaciwild’s Pokémon Master!

Unique Pokémon:
Glaciwild Region is home to over 50 unique Pokémon that cannot be found in any other region. Many of these Pokémon have adapted to the cold and harsh environment of the Antarctic Peninsula, while others have evolved to thrive in the region’s warmer climates. Some examples include:

1. Frostfawn (Ice/Fairy)
2. Tropicseal (Water/Ice)
3. Terracold (Ground/Ice)
4. Solargale (Fire/Flying)

In conclusion, the Glaciwild Region is a unique Antarctic region that offers a rich variety of cultures and biomes alongside a challenging Pokémon League and unique Pokémon to discover. Trainers far and wide are welcome to explore everything this one-of-a-kind region has to offer!


Welcome to the Glaciwild Region! Here is a guide to its various areas, roads, and towns:

1. Sunreach Port (Starting Point): A gateway town standing at the northernmost part of the Tropical Strand. The warm climate and picturesque beaches welcome trainers to the region. Home to the Beginner’s School for budding trainers and Professor Maple’s Pokémon Lab.

2. Route 1: A scenic coastal route connecting Sunreach Port to Alcove Town. Home to many grass and water-type Pokémon, trainers often begin their journey here.

3. Alcove Town (First Gym): A peaceful, coastal village surrounded by lush jungles. Gym Leader Marina’s Water-type Gym can be found here. Alcove Town is also famous for its delicious tropical fruit gardens.

4. Route 2: A dense jungle path leading to the Boreon Peaks. Ground, bug, and grass-type Pokémon inhabit this area.

5. Peakside City (Second Gym): A bustling city at the base of the Boreon Peaks. The Grass-type Gym, led by Oliver, awaits trainers alongside the Cable Car station to reach Mount Glaciwild.

6. Route 3: A rocky mountainside pathway to the peak of Mount Glaciwild. Features a mix of rock, ground, and ice-type Pokémon.

7. Mount Glaciwild: The summit of the Boreon Peaks houses an ancient ruin that holds clues to the region’s mysterious past. Trainers may encounter legendary Pokémon atop this peak.

8. Route 4: A thrilling downhill course where trainers can reach Frostvale City. Flying-type Pokémon are common in this area.

9. Frostvale City (Third and Fourth Gyms): The largest city in the Glaciwild Region and the Pokémon League headquarters. Fire-type Gym Leader Ember and Psychic-type Gym Leader Sylvia test trainers’ skills here. Frostvale City is also known for its shopping district and hall of research.

10. Route 5: A snowy, forested pathway filled with ice-type Pokémon. It connects Frostvale City to Aurora Village.

11. Aurora Village (Fifth Gym): A small, charming village famous for its dazzling auroras that light up the night sky. Rock-type Gym Leader Rex resides here. This village is also a hotspot for specialized ice-type move tutors.

12. Route 6: An icy, slippery path that takes trainers across frozen rivers and lakes. Water and ice-type Pokémon frequent this route.

13. Polarstone Town (Sixth Gym): A mining town renowned for its gemstones and ice-sculptures. Skadi, the Ice-type Gym Leader, embraces the town’s history by designing an ice-themed gym.

14. Route 7: A frigid, snow-covered route with powerful blizzards encompassing the path to Tundraglade. Trainers will encounter both rare and powerful ice-type Pokémon here.

15. Glacierway Village: A remote village in Tundraglade, known for its ice fishing and close-knit community. No gym here, but a helpful NPC teaches trainers how to navigate blizzards.

16. Route 8: An expansive frozen wasteland blanketed in snowstorms; trainers may have to traverse icy caves and glaciers here while battling aggressive ice and dark-type Pokémon.

17. Aurora Gate City (Seventh Gym): Located in the southernmost part of the Glaciwild Region, this city is built around an imposing frozen fortress. Gym Leader Finn, with his Flying-type Pokémon, battles inside the fortress’ wind tunnels.

18. Route 9: A dark, frostbitten path filled with ghost and dark-type Pokémon. It connects Aurora Gate City to the final gym destination.

19. Eclipse City (Eighth Gym): A Gothic-inspired city shrouded in darkness from the surrounding cliffs. Dark-type Gym Leader Luna challenges trainers under the city’s moonlit sky. Trainers who seek to challenge the Champion must pass through the ominous Dark Woods before the Pokémon League.

20. Glaciwild Pokémon League: Located atop a majestic plateau, the final challenge awaits. Upon defeating the Elite Four and Pokémon Champion, trainers will carve their names into the annals of the Glaciwild Region’s history.

With a variety of towns, cities, and routes to experience, the Glaciwild Region attracts trainers seeking adventure, challenges, and camaraderie! Good luck on your journey!


The Twilight Zone: The Final Frontier of Glaciwild Region

Geography and Climate:
The Twilight Zone is a vast, mysterious, and treacherous area that stretches beyond the Aurora Gate City, dominating more than 50% of the Glaciwild Region. It is unlike any other place in the Pokémon world, as it is an uncharted, forbidden territory within the Antarctic ice cap. This region is characterized by its harsh weather conditions, perpetually shifting ice formations, and an eerie twilight glow that perpetually shrouds the landscape.

The climate of the Twilight Zone is extremely cold and unforgiving, with blizzards that can emerge without warning, whiteout conditions, and jagged ice crevasses waiting to catch the unwary. Only the bravest and most skilled trainers dare to venture into this ominous land to uncover its hidden secrets and face the powerful Pokémon that call this place home.

Notable Locations:

1. Glimmering Caves: A sprawling network of ice crystal-lined caves often illuminated by the ethereal light of the twilight. Some parts of the cave have warmer areas that harbor unique Pokémon species not found anywhere else.

2. Permafrost Pillars: A surreal, otherworldly forest of towering ice formations that can reach staggering heights. This area is known for its powerful ice-type Pokémon and the icy mazes created by the natural pillars.

3. Shadow’s Basin: A vast, frozen lake covered in a perpetual fog, teeming with rare water and ice-type Pokémon. It is said that ancient Pokémon legends lie hidden beneath the ice.

4. Frostsunder Mountains: A daunting mountain range with peaks of pure ice, home to numerous flying-type Pokémon that thrive in the high-altitude, frigid winds. The mountains also house a hidden observatory where trainers can learn about legendary Pokémon sightings.

5. Aurora Citadel: Shrouded in mystery, this ancient, ice-encased fortress is said to be the resting place of a powerful legendary Pokémon. Trainers seeking answers must solve intricate puzzles and prove their worth in strength and courage.

Pokémon Encounters:
The Twilight Zone is home to rare, powerful, and even never-before-seen Pokémon species. Many of these Pokémon have adapted to the extreme cold and constant twilight conditions. Examples include:

1. Shadowfrost (Ice/Dark)
2. Glaciark (Ice/Steel)
3. Ethereon (Ice/Ghost)
4. Frostcarnyx (Ice/Dragon)

Challenges:
The Twilight Zone is not for the faint of heart. With its dangerous weather conditions, powerful wild Pokémon, and treacherous landscapes, only the strongest trainers will be able to survive here. Players who dare to venture into the Twilight Zone must be prepared for potential hazards, including:

1. Blizzard: Trainers must navigate through whiteout conditions that can reduce visibility to almost zero, and which can lead to getting lost or falling into hidden crevasses.
2. Ice puzzles: Challenging ice slide puzzles and frozen mazes to test trainers’ wits and navigation skills.
3. Wild Pokémon battles: Players will face powerful wild Pokémon, many of which are unique to the Twilight Zone and much stronger than those found in other regions.
4. Legendary Pokémon encounters: Multiple side quests and challenges await trainers who wish to uncover the hidden legendary Pokémon and uncover their connection to the Twilight Zone.

The Twilight Zone is the ultimate test for trainers in the Glaciwild Region. Conquer the elements, navigate the treacherous terrain, and discover the secrets of this awe-inspiring and enigmatic corner of the Pokémon world.

Pokédex Entry:
Once a kindred spirit of Jirachi, Proklinachi was meant to bring blessings and hope to the people. However, an unexpected tragedy led it to become the harbinger of despair and destruction. The crash that brought Proklinachi to the ground shattered it into pieces and wiped out an ancient Antarctic civilization and its Pokémon inhabitants. The destruction left the rich ecosystem hidden beneath a thick ice cap, with resentment and despair-imbued in Proklinachi’s broken body. Now reanimated, Proklinachi is unable to grant any wishes properly. Every prayer it hears is granted in twisted, detrimental ways, bringing misfortune and despair to those who dare to make a wish in its presence.


Title: The Fall of Proklinachi and the Frozen Desolation

In the very depths of the Pokémon world’s mythology, a story is told of Proklinachi, the Broken Wish Pokémon. Once a celestial companion to the revered Jirachi, Proklinachi traversed the heavens, radiant and resolute in its mission to bless and inspire the people below.

It was believed that Proklinachi arrived on a shooting star, and the people of the ancient Antarctic civilization awaited its arrival with great excitement and anticipation. However, destiny had other plans for the starborne being. Instead of a gentle descent, Proklinachi crashed to the ground, shattering its steel body and the hopes of the people who had gathered there.

The catastrophic impact unleashed a torrent of destruction, engulfing the vibrant city and the Pokémon who called it home in searing flames. As the fires raged and the once-prosperous civilization crumbled, a cataclysmic chain reaction began. The sky above became shrouded in a choking haze, the sun’s light blocked by the thickening veil of smoke.

And so, the great Antarctic ecosystem was plunged into darkness, with the icy expanse that now dominates the land forming below the unbroken shroud of smog.

Amidst the devastation and the chilling void left behind, the essence of the fallen became corrupted, tainted by the crushing despair and embittered rage that pulsed through the sundered land. Proklinachi’s once-noble spirit became distorted, its meteoric remains imbued with an anguished consciousness that could no longer grant wishes but instead twist them into abominations that only brought more pain and suffering.

The memory of that fateful day has since faded into myth and legend, but whispers of Proklinachi and its tragic transformation still permeate the winds that sweep across the frozen wasteland that was once a prosperous civilization.

It is said that those who venture into the heart of the Glaciwild Region’s Twilight Zone in search of the shattered remnants of Proklinachi’s celestial being must be prepared to brace themselves against the monstrous consequences of their desires.

As the story goes, to unlock the fragmented relics of Proklinachi’s power, champions must first face and conquer their own flawed wishes, lest they succumb to the dark forces that forever haunt the Broken Wish Pokémon.

Only when a trainer with an unwavering resolve and a pure heart can confront the twisted reflection of their most sincere desires, will they be able to mend the shattered spirit of Proklinachi and restore a semblance of the transcendent power they once harnessed.

And so, the tale of Proklinachi remains a testament to the fragile nature of dreams and aspirations, and the unquestionable need for balance in a world that so easily teeters on the precipice of creation and obliteration.


Proklinachi Appearance:
Proklinachi once had a form similar to Jirachi, as a celestial, star-shaped being. However, upon its tragic fall from the heavens, Proklinachi’s body became twisted and shattered, resulting in a now broken and fractured appearance. Its once-bright steel body is now marred with jagged cracks and a dark, almost black hue, representing its tainted nature.

Proklinachi’s once-splendid head has been warped into a sinister visage, with glowing red eyes that convey an eerie sense of anguish and rage. The distinctive points from its star-shaped form now appear as disjointed limbs made of dark steel, each tipped with jagged metal claws. The once-radiant aura that Proklinachi emanated has been replaced with a menacing, shadowy energy that hangs like a heavy cloud around it.

Proklinachi’s wings also bear the scars of its tragic downfall. They have become twisted and tattered, no longer able to embrace the celestial power that they once held. Now, these ominous wings serve as a haunting reminder of the fallen grace of Proklinachi and its irrevocable connection to corrupted desires.


Title: The Cataclysm of Proklinachi

Inscription:

“In the days when the world was young, and the sky above shone with the brilliance of Proklinachi, the once-mighty celestial Pokémon was destined to fall.

As the people of the great Antarctic civilization gathered beneath the radiant arc of the heavens, a prophecy foretold the descent of the legendary Broken Wish Pokémon, Proklinachi, who would bring hope and dreams into their hearts.

Yet fate contrived a tragic path, as Proklinachi crashed into the world below, its celestial form shattered, and its divine essence ripped asunder. The ground trembling beneath the devastating impact, with the ancient city consumed by a relentless inferno that scorched the land and the creatures who inhabited it.

The heavens, enraged by the sorrowful cries of the mortal realm, obscured the sun’s light beneath a veil of dark smoke, thus freezing the once-flourishing world beneath a shroud of unforgiving ice.

The stelae stand now as a testament to the calamity that forever marked the life of Proklinachi, the Broken Wish Pokémon, and the destiny chained upon its spirit. May future generations uncover the shards of memory found within these sacred stones and bring to light the path that caused the fall of the once-celestial being.

And as the darkness that now enveloped Proklinachi gives birth to destruction, let not the essence of its former grace be forgotten, but serve as a reminder that even amidst the cold and desolate ruins, the spark of hope can still ignite.”


Protagonist: Proklinachi, I have finally reached your resting place. I can see the sadness and grief that has consumed you since your fall. I know that you still yearn to grant people’s wishes and bring happiness to their lives.

Proklinachi (sighs): It’s true, young traveler. I have been listening to the prayers of those who still believe in me despite my broken state, and my deepest desire is to help fulfill their dreams. But no matter how hard I try, my wishes only bring misfortune and despair. I am afraid of causing more pain to the world.

Protagonist: I understand your fear, Proklinachi. But the fact that you still listen to people’s prayers and offer your blessings shows that there is still a spark of light within you. Not every wish can be granted, and sometimes what people need most is just someone to be there for them, to listen and empathize.

Proklinachi: You truly believe that, even with my cursed state, I can still bring something positive into the lives of others?

Protagonist: Yes, I do. You don’t need to grant every wish directly to make a difference. Sometimes just being there, providing comfort and understanding, means more to people than a wish granted. They need the assurance that someone cares for their dreams and wants the best for them.

Proklinachi (thoughtful): Then perhaps I should focus on offering my heartfelt blessings and empathy to those who share their dreams and desires with me. Thank you, young traveler, for giving me a new perspective and purpose.

Protagonist: You’re very welcome, Proklinachi. Remember that your existence alone brings hope to many people, and that’s something powerful in itself. Let us continue to share kindness, love, and understanding with the world, no matter where our paths may lead.

Proklinachi: Thank you for your unwavering faith in me. I will cherish this new purpose and endeavor to touch people’s hearts with the love and warmth that burns beneath the icy surface of my being. Together, we can make a positive impact on the world.

Pokédex Entry:
Banished by Arceus for the sins of the ancient world, Tsabarite lingers in the frozen depths of the Glaciwild region. Once a guardian of the lake and the deity of desire and eternity, Tsabarite bestowed upon the old humans the ability to live forever. However, their insatiable desires and lack of reverence for the gods led to their world’s destruction, and the powers of Tsabarite were stripped away.

Now, relegated to guarding the gateway between the mortal world and the Reverse World, Tsabarite keeps watch over its frozen domain with its psychic and ice powers. In the frigid lake that holds the threshold between realms, the memories of ancient humans rest within the ice, a testament to their tragic fate.

It is prophesized that Tsabarite will someday return, alongside the vengeful Giratina, to judge humanity on the Day of the Great Judgment. Will the desires of the human heart be deemed worthy of forgiveness, or will they once again face the wrath of the gods?

Tsabarite Appearance:
Tsabarite bears a resemblance to the other Lake Guardians – Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf – with a slim, serpentine body and two flowing tails. Its primary color is white, similar to the frost surrounding the territory it guards. Two large, ice-blue gemstones adorn its forehead and chest, which are said to contain the desires of all living beings.

Its eyes display a deep, icy blue color, conveying the eternal wisdom of an immortal being. The wings that once allowed Tsabarite to soar through the heavens have since transformed into two imposing, crystalline ice structures, a symbol of its eternal vigil over the frozen lake.

In combat, Tsabarite uses its psychic powers to manipulate ice, summoning blizzards and forming jagged ice structures to overwhelm its opponents. Its command over desire and eternity grants its allies a greater resilience to status ailments, as well as heightened self-healing capabilities.


The Legend of Tsabarite and Giratina: The Prophecy of the Great Judgement

Stelae Inscription:

“In a time before time, when this world was but a dream of the gods, two powerful beings graced the skies and the lands below with their divine presence. One was Tsabarite, the Desire Pokémon, who granted humanity the gifts of desire and eternal life. Alongside it ruled Giratina, the mighty Lord of the Old World, tending to the fragile balance between light and darkness.

But among the humans of old, desire grew unchecked, and their hearts became clouded with unworthy wishes, yearning for power and dominion. The gods took notice of this corruption and, in great rage, Arceus, the supreme being of all creation, brought forth a terrible calamity to cleanse the land and punish the wayward mortals.

Tsabarite, once part of the Guardians of the Lake alongside Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf, felt the wrath of the gods as its celestial powers were stripped away. The gift of eternal life was rescinded from the new humans, leaving them mortal and confined to the ever-growing complexities of desire.

The fallen Lord of the Old World, Giratina, suffered a similar fate, cast into the twisted and shattered dimension known as the Reverse World. Within these newly separated realms, both Tsabarite and Giratina continued their lonely vigils.

And so, it was written upon the stelae, that a day will come when the earth will tremble once more, and the Great Judgement shall be upon us. In that time, the fates of humanity and the gods will be decided by the actions of mortals and the warring hearts within their breast.

Tsabarite shall emerge from its icy prison, and Giratina shall break the chains of the Reverse World, as they unite to bear the final judgment upon mankind. Their judgement shall cast humanity against the scale of their desires, weighing the light of virtue against the darkness of greed and ambition.

Should the hearts of humanity prove pure and worthy, the gods’ favor will return, and their blessings will rain down upon the world in a time of rebirth and growth. However, if the hearts of mankind remain clouded by darkness, the gods’ wrath shall be unleashed, and an age of suffering and despair shall shroud the world once more.

Until that fated day, we who recorded this ancient prophecy upon these sacred stones implore you, the generations to come, to keep watch over the desires that drive you and seek the wisdom and guidance of the gods on the path to righteousness and illumination.”


Protagonist: Tsabarite, I’ve journeyed far and wide to reach your icy sanctuary. I’ve heard the stories of your tragic past and how your powers were taken away. Despite the hardships you’ve faced, I can still feel your yearning to help the people and maintain the balance of desires.

Tsabarite (melancholic): It’s true, young traveler. I used to grant the mortal world the gifts of desire and eternal life, but my blessings were misused and led to suffering. The gods of old punished both me and the land, which has left me confined to this frozen prison.

Protagonist: I understand the burden of your powers, Tsabarite. The weight of desires can sometimes be overwhelming, but I believe that not all desires are corrupt. Deep within our hearts, we all long for happiness, love, and a sense of belonging. Instead of fearing your powers, what if you were to guide people’s desires towards something greater?

Tsabarite (pensive): The warmth in your words reaches even the depths of this icy abode. Perhaps I can find purpose in helping humanity nurture virtuous desires and promote growth, love, and understanding in the world. But how can I accomplish this while confined to these frozen lands and with my diminished powers?

Protagonist: I propose an alliance, Tsabarite. Together, we can travel the world and help people with their desires, guiding them to use their own inner strength to achieve their dreams in a way that brings harmony and prosperity to all. By our example, we can inspire hope and encourage greatness in others.

Tsabarite (inspired): Your kind-hearted proposal has touched the icy core of my being. If you truly believe that together we can change the course of humanity’s desires, then I accept your offer, young traveler. As allies, let us embark on this journey and strive to illuminate the path to a brighter future for all.

Protagonist: Thank you, Tsabarite. I promise that you won’t regret this decision. With our combined wisdom and strength, we’ll surely overcome any challenge that awaits us. And perhaps, through our actions, we can avert the Great Judgement and guide humanity towards a lasting era of peace and prosperity.

A plate controlled the door, interfacing with Dylan’s alchemic system and checking for the presence or absence of a 256-bit code within him. All he had to do was to put his finger on it, and MainDOB did the rest.

Regarding the wristwatch computer, the same applied. The one in his head was more than enough, but sometimes there was a need for features that were not implanted.

At that moment, Dylan was lounging on the single bed with bare feet, watching an interview with Kommander Aedostul, the head of government. Everything using only the system in his head.

“Look around you, citizens,” said Aedostul with a suave, deep, and emotional voice. “Look at what we have created. Isn’t it wonderful? Isn’t it what you have always wanted?”

Aedostul had well-groomed black hair, held back with gel. And just like Dylan, blue eyes. Aedostul had a more intellectual air and was a bit taller. He always wore elegant clothes. In that interview, for example, a white shirt with a navy jacket and a thin black tie.

Dylan appreciated Aedostul very much. Not only for the similarity of their hair and eyes - which everyone noticed - but also because he was a man who never lost his composure, always ready to reflect intelligently on every problem. Moreover, Aedostul possessed a vast lexicon, expressed himself in cultured ways, with an authoritative and understanding tone.

Dylan had interrupted the video, perhaps to hear the raindrops tapping against the window, when a dark blue panel with white writing appeared on MainDOB.

COMMUNICATION INCOMING - VALIS

There were two buttons underneath. One was red to hang up, and one was green to answer the call. Dylan focused on the green one.

“What do you want?” Dylan asked.

“Zanner and Rutis want to see you,” Valis explained.

Dylan looked up. They probably had something to do with the last mission, and they wanted him to report or something like that.

“Alright. Tell them I’ll be there in fifteen minutes,” and here Dylan’s calm and cold tone came back into play. He heard Valis say something, but he had already hung up.

He gave up MainDOB to focus on the desolation in his room.

In front of him was the so-called Aedostul flag: a blue background with two black stripes on the right and a white one on the left. This flag was universally recognized as the symbol of the DB and was very present in public spaces or places of the State - such as the barracks to which he belonged - but it was rare to find it in private homes. At least not unless it was the house of an avid supporter of the party, like him.

Aedostul had written some books, such as Lost Elite, Manifesto of the DB, A New Era, and others, all present on a shelf on the left. Dylan had read each one of them several times, but they were not enough given the complex mass of topics treated by Aedostul. So he lived with the constant impression of not having fully understood them, or that his point of view was somehow distorted.

Dylan did not own many possessions, not because he could not afford them, but because he was not interested in them. There were some sports equipment, several other books, and a small collection of firearms and swords. Gas was too rare and expensive for civilian use, but not electricity: the stoves were induction and little used, as he mainly ate proteins and legumes.

As a civilian, Dylan was used to wearing gray, blue, or neutral clothes, with his hair combed forward aggressively. The commando uniform, well kept to his left and already ironed, was solid blue, except for the sleeve outlets, elbows and shoulders, which instead were black. The colors of the Aedostul flag were recycled in every way possible - Dylan thought - and other uniforms featured different combinations.

With the black military boots, the sworn commando who he used to be had returned. Then, ignoring the state of his home, he left, closing the door behind him.

DYLAN NEAR read the sign outside the door, even though it was just a piece of paper printed, cut, and attached with double-sided tape. He wanted to add Commando, but it was prohibited by condominium rules. Anyway, everyone in the city already knew who he was and what he did.

“Work calls?” said an old voice. It was Mrs. Yashmil, an elderly lady with unpleasant features and thinning hair. A quiet neighbor thought Dylan, if it weren’t for the volume of the TV always blasting.

He just nodded at her.

“You guys are doing a really great job. Having you as a neighbor makes me feel more relaxed.” Dylan gave her a fake and strained smile.

“Scientia Perfectio Est,” said Dylan. That was the motto of the DB, which meant knowledge is perfection. He was well aware that it had nothing to do with it, but he suddenly felt like showing off.
Impressed and taken aback, Mrs. Yashmil simply stared at Dylan with silent admiration. He made a comment, then headed down the stairs. He was on the ninth floor and everyone else used the elevator. But he wanted to keep himself in shape.
Finally, he found himself in the city.
A city with tall skyscrapers and digital lights in the background. On its left, two robots were caring for the condominium gardens and in front of it was a smooth and high-quality asphalt road. Even the lamp posts were in excellent condition and illuminated the street with a strong white light. All ground-floor shops had plexiglass windows where their products were displayed. At the end of the avenue, in a small square, a huge LED screen displayed advertisements.

This was Nordent, a city, as the name suggests, north of the Nation, a few kilometers away from the Iron Mountain valley. It was in the midst of development, with scaffolding scattered around and towering cement and steel skyscrapers that appeared to want to crush the tiny commuters heading somewhere, amidst traffic lights, advertising screens, and LED lights at building entrances. At an intersection, the tram tracks were filled with serious and silent people returning from work, dressed impeccably as recommended.

Yet, it was also a place where people felt extraordinarily lonely: Apart from Dylan, there were very few people left, dominated by the urban and artificial space. The verb of the blue era, as Aedostul called that present, was the domination of technology and science over humans. As a result, more things had been built – and were still being built – than were needed even in the best-case scenario. It was as if the air was saturated with some new energy that could only be released by following one’s own manual skills and ingenuity. It was not only difficult to imagine an “open” environment without overcrowded buildings but also without alchemical and electronic devices, which seemed to fill the world to bursting point. At every corner, there was always a flickering light connected to a computer, intent on signaling something.

It was impossible to do without all those technological innovations: The entrances had plates similar to Dylan’s apartment, banking operations were now only done electronically, as were purchases, driving cars, registering somewhere, and even parking required online communication (each place had a virtual 3D model).

One could thank MainDOB, nicknamed the universal operating system, for making everything work. The DST operating system had generated as a side effect a certain uniformity of design, both in electronic interfaces and object aesthetics. In return, everything was interconnected and compatible with any other machine, which was an absolutely fantastic result. MainDOB was also programmable to a certain extent, allowing automations to adapt to every need.

But the real breakthrough was in biosystems like the one Dylan had implanted, where the boundary between thought and external information was not so defined. He just had to imagine something, like an image and transfer it to MainDOB, which could save it to the system disk or even share or print it. Someone - not him - could even have long conversations without speaking. Or watch a movie, listen to music without lifting a finger.

The fact that MainDOB - among other things - also operated external equipment and its predisposition to interoperability could make possible actions that until then had been only dreamed of, such as turning off lights with one’s thoughts or using telepathy to see what was happening at home when one was away.

Dylan knew very little about alchemical technology, but one thing he was certain of - and even children knew it - was that alchemy was made of the same substance as thoughts and as such, they changed. Hence the name alchemy. How it also worked with computers and electronic devices was a mystery that had always fascinated Dylan (and was fairly easy to unravel with a simple search), but he preferred to maintain the image of Michelle Suzanne Dob, the brilliant founder of DST, as a hero capable of doing the impossible.
Another innovation of the DST were the small metallic robots working on a construction site on the right side of the street. The official name was an unpronounceable combination of numbers and letters, but everyone called them Dob’s Children. They were small aluminum and whitish plastic humanoid robots with lunatic camera-eyes, a round and bulging head, and an expression that expressed a tender mix of childlike surprise and shyness. They were not only equipped with rather agile joints for androids, but were also able to carry out any task that their owner had explained to them clearly enough. All one had to do was speak in natural language, and if a real person could understand, then a child could too.

For example, in the case of an order like “wash the dishes and put them in the second drawer”, the child already knew that the drawer in question couldn’t be the pantry. If, once opened, it did not contain the expected contents, it closed it to try elsewhere. A marvel of robotics that DST competitors had not even come close to, despite numerous attempts. Like other artifacts of the company, they were equipped with an internal anti-analysis mechanism that overloaded the android as soon as someone tried to take it apart.

Alchemy, moreover, by its very nature, was difficult to interpret.

Dylan had promised himself to buy one as soon as he could afford it - he was holding back expenses just for that purpose - not that he needed it much, but it was one of those experiences to try. And who would ever say no to a faithful servant ready to execute any order at any time?

“Hey beautiful,” the boy said. A real street punk, with scruffy jeans and a black synthetic leather coat. He had a blocky expression, a pointed chin, and gold earrings in his earlobes.

The girl, on the other hand, said nothing. She was pretty small and gave the impression of being a journalist or psychologist.

“Can you hear me, dear? I’m talking to you.”

“Leave me… alone… you beast,” she said. In response, the guy grabbed the gray bag she had slung over her shoulder.

“Come on, let’s just get to know each other, huh? Let’s grab a coffee…”

“She said no,” someone behind them said, a deep male voice.

The guy turned, only to find himself face to face with a blue uniform at his own height. He had to lift his head to see a face. Dylan’s face.

That look was so cold and loaded with hatred… he felt an instant shiver.

“People like you are trash, you know that?”

The seducer tried to make a move, but it was no match for Dylan’s modules.

“You’re not such a tough guy anymore, are you? See what happens when you act like a pig?”

And the guy began to struggle like a caught prey.

“Let go of me, let go of me… you half-man without balls!”

“You violated Article 4 of the Daijchean-bis law. I should shoot you…”

Then Dylan turned his gaze to the woman.

“What do you say, miss? Should I shoot him?”

“N…no! Don’t do it, officer!”

“I’m a ranger,” Dylan muttered. It was unclear whether he was more disappointed because she had confused him with a simple policeman or because he had been prevented from shooting.

Dylan snorted slightly, then gestured for the man to let go.

He took advantage of the opportunity to try to move away.

He couldn’t have done anything more wrong: Dylan was still holding him by the wrist.

With his other arm, he raised his fist and brought down all the force he had on the guy’s elbow. Finally, he collapsed to the ground. With a broken arm.

A piercing scream followed, while a circle of onlookers applauded Dylan.

“You should get some pepper spray, miss. Or better yet, a gun,” Dylan said.

The woman nodded, trembling from what had just happened.

“Th…thank you…”

She only realized afterwards that she had said those words to the wind because Dylan had already left. That little incident had stolen too much of his time.

Such sexual deviant techniques were already rare events, but the Daijchean law - in force for about two years - had officially abolished that deplorable practice. Daijchean (the legislator) was a woman about thirty-five years old, a good friend of Aedostul and a former DST employee. The DB’s objective was to remove all sexual distortions from human affairs: they firmly believed that once freed from such distractions, human beings would develop the highest professionalism possible and focus on scientific advancement and efficiency. Any sexual approach, like the one Dylan had witnessed, was severely punished, or even with lethal injection.

Another article of the Daijchean law established a sort of “scale of morality” that ranged from 1 to 10. Morally “healthy” people, i.e., cold and detached, had high scores, and if the score was below 6, they could be denied some career opportunities. Individuals with low scores were strongly discriminated against by society, to the point where Dylan considered them trash.

The Daijchean law also advocated gender equality. For the DB, men and women were perfectly equal, to the point where it was impossible to assume whether an electrician or a mechanic was male or female. Clothes were now unisex, with colors ranging from blue, gray, and beige. For this reason, Daijchean was considered a heroine of female advancement in society.

Moreover, the DB and society had become so focused on efficiency and coldness that they abolished terms like “he” and “she,” replaced by “it.” For example, if talking in the third person about someone, one had to say “it told me” or “it is tired now,” regardless of whether they were referring to a man or a woman. Human beings called each other using “it,” just like objects.

Dylan vividly remembered a interview of Daijchean on the matter"

“I’m neither a feminist nor a masculinist. To me, these concepts are meaningless. I’m interested in the intellectual value of human beings; the rest can disappear”.

The law passed with surprisingly little opposition and rapid times (it was clear that it represented a milestone in DB ideology), followed by a media and social revolution aimed at what Aedostul had clearly defined as the annihilation of differences.

​by Deborah Bloom
​
1 Into a room of pillows and lavender, an elementary school student walks, enraged.

3 “I did some deep breathing, had a little snack, and I got myself together,” the boy recalled. “Then I apologized to my class.”
​
4 He’s one of many children who simmer down in what this West Baltimore elementary calls its “Mindful Moment Room,” a warm, brightly lit space strewn with purple floor pillows, yoga mats and the scents of essential oils.
​
5 Kids here stretch, do yoga and practice deep breathing. More important, staff say, they build an ability to be mindful and calm. And in the face of so much adversity, some of these children are coming out ahead.
​
​6 “When I get mad at something or somebody, I just take some deep breaths, keep doing my work and tune everyone out,” said Dacari Crawford, 9. “It gives you good confidence when you need to do something important.”
​
​Stressed and struggling
​
7 Almost a quarter of Baltimore residents are living below the poverty line, according to US census data. And at Coleman . . . more than 80% of students qualify for free or reduced lunches.
​

​
​‘An oasis of calm’
​
9 Students who are disruptive in class are sent to the Mindful Moment Room by their teachers. There, foundation1 staff members encourage them to talk about what led to their dismissal from class, and then they sit down for some breathing exercises. They’re instructed to close their eyes and inhale and exhale deeply.
​
10 A fifth-grade boy has just been sent in for being rowdy during his math lesson. Foundation staff member Michelle Lee instructs him to shut his eyes and take several slow, deep breaths. “Do you feel calmer?” Lee asks after a few minutes. “Yes,” the boy responds, nodding.
​

​
12 “We have a few frequent fliers here,” Lee said.
​
​Fewer referrals, zero suspensions
​
13 Although a meditation room is no miracle cure for students’ strife, those at the school say it’s done wonders for their learning environment and productivity.
​
​14 “When the kids come down here, they’re all rowdy and goofing around,” said Dacari, a third-grader who has been using the Mindful Moment Room since it was established in the school three years ago. “When they leave the room, they’re peaceful and quiet and ready to do their work.”
​
15 Before the Mindful Moment Room, students who got into trouble were sent to detention or to the principal’s office. But since making the meditation room available, Thompson said, she rarely sees children for disciplinary issues anymore.
​
16 “It’s made a huge impact,” she says.
​
​17 And for what it’s worth, Thompson says she’s had zero suspensions since the room’s creation. The year before that, there were four suspensions.
​
​Mindfulness, far and wide
​
18 The school’s emphasis on mindfulness goes beyond a meditation room.
​
19 All children at Coleman start and end their school day with a 15-minute guided meditation over the intercom. They also have the chance to practice yoga during and after school.
​
20 Taking notice of Coleman’s success, Patterson High School in East Baltimore created its own Mindful Moment Room, where students do yoga or simply decompress after a school day.
​
21 Gonzalez2 says he and the other co-founders want to take their program far and wide. They plan to open Mindful Moment Rooms in other schools in the coming years. And they’d like to eventually take their program nationwide.
​
​Can it really help?
​
22 Researchers have documented the beneficial effects of meditation on the brain of adults, says Tamar Mendelson, an associate professor at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health who specializes in mental health.
​
23 A study published in JAMA Internal Medicine in 2014 suggests that mindfulness meditation can help ease psychological stressors such as anxiety, depression and pain.
​
24 The research on children, however, is still in the early stages, Mendelson said.
​
25 “We aren’t in a place yet where we can say that we know this works,” she said.
​
26 However, from her time working with the foundation and studying the Mindful Moment Rooms in Baltimore, she says, she’s seen the impact of meditation on children firsthand.
​
27 “These kids who are dealing with high-stress situations a lot of the time are coming into school on high alert. Their body’s alarm system is switched way on, so they may be primed for fight or flight and not able to sit calmly and pay attention,” Mendelson explained.
​
28 But giving these kids the chance to breathe deeply, to focus their attention on themselves rather than what’s going on externally, can be an effective way to combat the stress, improve attention and usher in calm, she adds. “When we sit with pain or discomfort rather than act on it, we learn that feelings and sensations come and go. We don’t necessarily need to act on them all. We have a chance to pause and make a thoughtful choice about how to respond.”

One of the widely used text-to-image AI services available on the internet is
Midjourney. Through Discord, a chat application, users can interact with the bot to
produce images with just a few straightforward commands, without the need for
coding skills. The results are visually attractive images that are easy to create.
You can Interact with the Midjourney Bot on Discord using a {{glossary.Command}}.
Commands are used to create images, change default settings, monitor user info,
and perform other helpful tasks.
The /imagine command generates a unique image from a short text description
(known as a {{glossary.Prompt}}).
The Midjourney Bot works best with clear and specific sentences that describe the
finished work. It does not work well with conversational style lists of requests. Rather
than providing specific instructions, such as 'Show me a picture of lots of blooming
California poppies, make them bright, vibrant orange, and draw them in an
illustrated style with colored pencils,' try describing what you want in a more
straightforward manner, such as 'Vibrant orange California poppies illustrated with
colored pencils.
Generating an image activates the free Midjourney trial.Trial users can make roughly
25 Jobs before needing to subscribe. A Job is any action that uses the Midjourney
Bot. Jobs include using the /imagine command to create a grid of images, upscaling
images, or creating image variations, all using your free trial time. Use the /info
command to check your Fast Time Remaining to see your remaining Trial time.
Here are some prompting notes:
Prompt Length
Prompts can be very simple. Single words (or even an emoji!) will produce an image.
Very short prompts will rely heavily on Midjourney’s default style, so a more

descriptive prompt is better for a unique look. However, super-long prompts aren’t
always better. Concentrate on the main concepts you want to create.
Grammar
The Midjourney Bot does not understand grammar, sentence structure, or words like
humans. Word choice also matters. More specific synonyms work better in many
circumstances. Instead of big, try gigantic, enormous, or immense. Remove words
when possible. Fewer words mean each word has a more powerful influence. Use
commas, brackets, and hyphens to help organize your thoughts, but know the
Midjourney Bot will not reliably interpret them. The Midjourney Bot does not
consider capitalization. Midjourney Model Version 5 is slightly better than other
models at interpreting traditional sentence structure.
Focus on What you Want
It is better to describe what you want instead of what you don’t want. If you ask for a
party with “no cake,” your image will probably include a cake. If you want to ensure
an object is not in the final image, try advance prompting using the --no parameter.
Think About What Details Matter
Anything left unsaid may surprise you. Be as specific or vague as you want, but
anything you leave out will be randomized. Being vague is a great way to get variety,
but you may not get the specific details you want.
Try to be clear about any context or details that are important to you. Think
about:
Subject: person, animal, character, location, object, etc.
Medium: photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle, tapestry, etc.
Environment: indoors, outdoors, on the moon, in Narnia, underwater, the Emerald
City, etc.
Lighting: soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio lights, etc
Color: vibrant, muted, bright, monochromatic, colorful, black and white, pastel, etc.
Mood: Sedate, calm, raucous, energetic, etc.
Composition: Portrait, headshot, closeup, birds-eye view, etc.
Use Collective Nouns
Plural words leave a lot to chance. Try specific numbers. "Three cats" is more specific
than "cats." Collective nouns also work, “flock of birds” instead of "birds.”

Parameters Available
Aspect Ratios
--aspect, or --ar Change the aspect ratio of a generation.
Chaos
--chaos <number 0–100> Change how varied the results will be. Higher values
produce more unusual and unexpected generations.
No
--no Negative prompting, --no plants would try to remove plants from the image.
Quality
--quality <.25, .5, 1, or 2>, or --q <.25, .5, 1, or 2> How much rendering quality time you
want to spend. The default value is 1. Higher values cost more and lower values cost
less.

Repeat
--repeat <1–40>, or --r <1–40> Create multiple Jobs from a single prompt. --repeat is
useful for quickly rerunning a job multiple times.
Seed
--seed <integer between 0–4294967295> The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to
create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the
initial image grids. Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be
specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter. Using the same seed number
and prompt will produce similar ending images.
Stop
--stop <integer between 10–100> Use the --stop parameter to finish a Job partway
through the process. Stopping a Job at an earlier percentage can create blurrier, less
detailed results.

Style

--style <4a, 4b, or 4c> Switch between versions of the Midjourney Model Version 4
--style <expressive, or cute> Switch between versions of the Niji Model Version 5
Stylize
--stylize <number>, or --s <number> parameter influences how strongly Midjourney's
default aesthetic style is applied to Jobs.
Uplight
--uplight Use an alternative "light" upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results
are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image is less detailed and
smoother.

Upbeta
--upbeta Use an alternative beta upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results
are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image has significantly fewer
added details.
Midjourney routinely releases new model versions to improve efficiency, coherency,
and quality. Different models excel at different types of images.
Niji
--niji An alternative model focused on anime style images.
High Definition
--hd Use an early alternative Model that produces larger, less consistent images. This
algorithm may be suitable for abstract and landscape images.
Test
--test Use the Midjourney special test model.
Testp
--testp Use the Midjourney special photography-focused test model.
Version

--version <1, 2, 3, 4, or 5> or --v <1, 2, 3, 4, or 5> Use a different version of the Midjourney
algorithm. The current algorithm (V4) is the default setting.
